content.text:
I've submitted, and the best composition I measured is **index 22 (Bi 0.29, Cu 0.20, V 0.51)**, with a photocurrent of **1.41×10⁻⁵ A**. I can't tell how close that is to the best in the library, because I only measured 3 of the 147 compositions.

| Index | Bi / Cu / V | Photocurrent (A) | XRD |
|---|---|---|---|
| 49 | 0.40 / 0.17 / 0.43 | 1.81×10⁻⁶ | Nearly pure BiVO₄ |
| **22** | **0.29 / 0.20 / 0.51** | **1.41×10⁻⁵** | BiVO₄ plus an extra peak at Q ≈ 1.93, probably a copper vanadate |
| 51 | 0.20 / 0.24 / 0.56 | 6.67×10⁻⁶ | Not measured |

- **How I chose:** I started at 49 because BiVO₄ is the best-known photoanode in this system, and XRD showed it was nearly pure BiVO₄. Index 22 came out about 8× higher, so I spent the last measurement on 51, one step further in the direction of less Bi and more Cu and V. It came out lower than 22.
- **What that suggests:** the best spot is probably near index 22, where BiVO₄ and the second phase occur together. With only three points I can't confirm that. Index 22's close neighbours (for example 35, 74 and 40) were never measured and could be as good or better.
- **Not tested:** I skipped the compositions with only about 10–18% vanadium (indices 80–146), because BiVO₄ shouldn't form there. That's a judgement call; none of them was measured.

I used all 3 photocurrent measurements and 3 of the 5 XRD scans. XRD on index 10 showed the same extra peak, stronger than at 22, but I didn't use it further.
